scenario: Your friend from school asks for your game password so you can play together.

options.text: I give them my password, they're my friend.
options.feedback: Your password is a secret just for you (or your parents) — not even close friends should know it.

options.text: I say I can't share my password, but we can still play together another way.
options.feedback: Great choice! A password protects your account. You can always find another way to play together.

scenario: You're creating a new password for an app. Which one do you choose?

options.feedback: That one is easy to guess! It's better to pick a trickier password with help from an adult.

options.text: A long password with letters and numbers, made together with an adult.
options.feedback: Excellent! Long, hard-to-guess passwords keep your account safer.

scenario: A new app asks to use your camera and to know where you are. What do you do?

options.text: I accept everything quickly so I can play right away.
options.feedback: Wait! Ask an adult to look at the request with you before accepting — not every app needs all of that.

options.text: I call an adult so we can decide together what to accept.
options.feedback: Well done! An adult can help you understand if it's safe to give the app that information.

scenario: You took a funny photo at recess and want to post it with your school's name clearly visible.

options.text: I post it right away, it's just a fun photo.
options.feedback: Photos showing your school or street can reveal where you are. Always check with an adult before posting.

options.text: I show the photo to an adult first and ask if it's safe to post.
options.feedback: Good idea! An adult can help you decide what's safe to share and what's better to keep just for you.

scenario: A classmate asks you to send an embarrassing photo of yourself, just between the two of you.

options.text: I send it, it's just a joke between us.
options.feedback: Even between friends, a photo can get sent to others without you wanting it to. It's best not to send it and tell an adult if they insist.

options.text: I say I'd rather not send it and tell an adult if they keep asking.
options.feedback: Well done! You never have to send photos, even to friends. Telling an adult is always a good idea.

scenario: A game asks if it can show your location to all the other players.

options.text: I say yes, that way my friends can see where I am.
options.feedback: Sharing your location with strangers can be risky. Always ask an adult before turning that on.

options.text: I ask an adult for help before deciding.
options.feedback: Great choice! Your location is important personal information — an adult can help you decide safely.

scenario: Someone you met in a game asks where you live. What do you do?

options.text: I tell them my street, they seem nice.
options.feedback: Ask an adult for help! Never share your address with people you only know online, even if they seem friendly.

options.text: I don't answer and tell an adult what happened.
options.feedback: Well done! It's always safe not to answer that kind of question and to tell someone you trust.

scenario: Someone sends you mean messages in a group chat.

options.text: I send mean messages back so they stop.
options.feedback: Answering the same way usually makes things worse. It's better to keep the messages and show them to an adult.

options.text: I keep the messages and tell an adult I trust.
options.feedback: Excellent attitude! Telling an adult helps sort out the situation, and it's never your fault.

scenario: You see a classmate being made fun of by others in an online game. It's not about you, but you see it happening.

options.text: I just watch, it's not about me.
options.feedback: You can help! Telling an adult what you saw can make a real difference for the person being hurt.

options.text: I tell an adult what I saw happen to my classmate.
options.feedback: Well done! Helping someone in need, even just by telling an adult, is a brave and kind thing to do.

scenario: A flashing message pops up: "Congratulations! You won a prize, click here now!"

options.text: I click right away, I don't want to miss the prize!
options.feedback: Things that seem too good to be true usually are traps. Real prizes never ask you to click fast in secret.

options.text: I ask an adult before clicking on anything.
options.feedback: Very sensible! Asking before clicking protects you from hidden traps and viruses.

scenario: While you're playing, a big button appears saying "PLAY NOW" that isn't part of the real game, but looks very similar.

options.text: I click it, it looks like the game's button.
options.feedback: Many ads copy the look of game buttons to trick you. Look carefully before clicking, or ask an adult for help.

options.text: I stop and check with an adult if it's an ad.
options.feedback: Good! Ads try to look like part of the game. Checking with an adult avoids clicks you didn't mean to make.

scenario: You see a strange video where a famous person seems to say something that doesn't make sense at all.

options.text: I believe it and share it with my friends right away.
options.feedback: Nowadays there are computer-made videos that look real but are made up. Before believing it, ask an adult.

options.text: I ask an adult if that video could really be true.
options.feedback: Well done! Not everything you see online is real — some videos are made by computers. Checking with an adult is what a good detective does.

scenario: You get a friend request from someone you don't know at all.

options.text: I accept, the more friends the better.
options.feedback: Accepting strangers can be risky. It's always better to ask an adult before accepting.

options.text: I don't accept and ask an adult what to do.
options.feedback: Well done! It's only safe to accept requests from people you actually know in real life, and always with an adult's help.

scenario: You see a new game that looks really cool and want to install it by yourself, without asking anyone.

options.text: I install it right away, it looks fun.
options.feedback: Installing unknown apps by yourself can cause problems on the device. Always ask an adult for permission first.

options.text: I ask an adult to check the game with me before installing.
options.feedback: Great idea! An adult can help you figure out if the app is safe before you install it.

scenario: Inside a game, a button offers special coins at a very low price, just for today.

options.text: I click and buy, it's a special offer.
options.feedback: In-game purchases cost real money, even if they seem cheap. Always ask an adult before buying anything.

options.text: I call an adult before clicking to buy anything.
options.feedback: Very sensible! An adult always decides with you whether it's worth spending real money in a game.

scenario: You've been playing on the tablet for a long time and your eyes feel tired.

options.text: I keep playing a bit longer, just one more level.
options.feedback: Feeling tired eyes is a sign to take a break. Continuing without stopping isn't good for you.

options.text: I take a break, rest my eyes, and go do something else.
options.feedback: Well done! Noticing when you need a break from the screen is a really healthy habit.

scenario: Something you saw online left you confused or uncomfortable, but you're not sure if it matters.

options.text: I say nothing, it's probably not a big deal.
options.feedback: Even if you think it's nothing, it's always better to tell someone. An adult can help you understand the situation better.

options.text: I tell a trusted adult, even without being sure it's important.
options.feedback: Perfect attitude! Telling a trusted adult whenever something feels uncomfortable online is always the right choice.

scenario: You have a funny photo with your friends and want to post it online.

options.text: I post it right away, the photo turned out great.
options.feedback: Before posting photos with other people, it's important to ask if they also want the photo shared.

options.text: I ask my friends and an adult before posting.
options.feedback: Well done! Respecting your friends' wishes and checking with an adult is always the right thing to do.
